plain_description: DeepSeek-R1 delivers OpenAI-o1-class reasoning performance in math, code, and logic tasks — now open-source and MIT-licensed. It uses reinforcement learning to teach models to think step-by-step, and distilled versions run on hardware as small as 1.5B parameters. The bottom line: production-grade reasoning without the proprietary price tag.
technical_description: DeepSeek-R1 is a first-generation reasoning LLM trained via large-scale reinforcement learning (RL) on a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) base model (DeepSeek-V3-Base, 671B total / 37B activated parameters, 128K context). The pipeline alternates two RL stages (reasoning-pattern discovery and human-preference alignment) with two SFT stages (seed data for reasoning and non-reasoning capabilities). The model exposes an OpenAI-compatible REST API at platform.deepseek.com and a chat UI at chat.deepseek.com. Distilled dense variants (1.5B–70B) based on Qwen2.5 and Llama-3 are provided for local inference via vLLM or SGLang. Recommended temperature is 0.5–0.7; system prompts should be avoided.
title: DeepSeek-R1

plain_description: DeepSeek-V3 is a state-of-the-art open-source language model that delivers performance rivaling the best closed-source models at a fraction of the training cost. It excels at reasoning, coding, math, and multilingual tasks, making it a powerful foundation for building AI applications.
technical_description: DeepSeek-V3 is a 671B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 37B activated parameters per token, using Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE architectures. It employs an auxiliary-loss-free load balancing strategy and a Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) training objective. The model was pre-trained on 14.8 trillion tokens using an FP8 mixed precision training framework. Inference is supported via multiple community frameworks including SGLang, vLLM, LMDeploy, TensorRT-LLM, and LightLLM, with support for FP8, BF16, and INT4/8 quantization. The model supports a 128K context window and is available as both a base and chat variant.
title: DeepSeek-V3

plain_description: Gemma gives you Google-grade open-weights LLMs to build AI into your products without vendor lock-in. It handles multi-modal conversations combining text and images and can be fine-tuned on your own data. Runs on your own infrastructure with no external API dependency.
technical_description: Gemma is a JAX-based library for using and fine-tuning Google DeepMind's family of open-weights large language models. The Python package provides a ChatSampler API for multi-turn, multi-modal conversations and supports fine-tuning via LoRA adapters. Models are available in multiple sizes (2B to 7B+) and run on CPU, GPU, or TPU hardware. Includes Colab notebooks for sampling, multi-modal inference, and fine-tuning workflows.
title: Gemma

plain_description: The big picture: Meta's Llama 3 gives businesses and creators access to powerful large language models (8B to 70B parameters) for building AI applications. Here's why it matters: you can run pre-trained and instruction-tuned models locally for text generation and chat, with model weights and inference code provided. The bottom line: this repo is deprecated in favor of the newer Llama 3.1 / Llama Stack ecosystem.
technical_description: This repository provides model weights and inference code for Meta Llama 3, a family of auto-regressive language models ranging from 8B to 70B parameters. It supports pre-trained (base) and instruction-tuned variants with sequence lengths up to 8192 tokens. Inference requires PyTorch with CUDA and uses torchrun with model parallelism (MP=1 for 8B, MP=8 for 70B). The codebase includes example scripts for text completion and chat completion with a specific chat format using special tokens. Models are distributed as native weights downloadable via a signed URL or Hugging Face, and the repo is deprecated in favor of the consolidated Llama Stack repositories.
title: Llama 3

plain_description: OLMo gives AI researchers and enterprises a complete open-source stack to train, fine-tune, and deploy state-of-the-art language models from 1B to 32B parameters. It provides the code, configs, and checkpoints needed to reproduce production-grade LLMs without starting from scratch. The bottom line: skip building your own training infrastructure and use a proven, fully open platform.
technical_description: OLMo is a Python library for training, evaluating, and serving large language models using PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers. It implements a two-stage pretraining pipeline that trains on web-scale data followed by curated high-quality data, with distributed training orchestrated via torchrun and YAML-based configuration files. The library supports model quantization through bitsandbytes, publishes checkpoints in both native and Hugging Face formats, and includes an OpenAI-compatible API server deployable on Modal.com. Inference is available via the Hugging Face transformers API with text-generation pipeline support.
title: OLMo

plain_description: The big picture: Phi-3 Mini brings enterprise-grade AI language capabilities to your applications without requiring massive infrastructure — it is a compact model that delivers strong reasoning, coding, and long-context analysis on cost-effective hardware. Why it matters: At 3.8 billion parameters, it outperforms many larger models while using significantly less computing power and memory. The bottom line: Get production-ready AI with lower costs and simpler deployment.
technical_description: Phi-3-Mini-128K-Instruct is a 3.8 billion-parameter, dense decoder-only Transformer model for text generation. It supports up to 128K tokens of context and has been post-trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and direct preference optimization (DPO) for instruction-following and safety alignment. The model integrates with HuggingFace Transformers (v4.41.3+) and is distributed in safetensors format with ONNX, GGUF, and PyTorch variants available. It uses Flash Attention for inference on NVIDIA GPUs (A100, A6000, H100) and can run on CPU and mobile devices via ONNX Runtime. The model supports chat-format prompting with system, user, and assistant roles, and is capable of code generation, long-document understanding, reasoning, and structured output. Fine-tuning is supported via TRL and Accelerate; int4 quantization (AWQ, RTN) is available through ONNX-format models.
title: Phi-3 Mini 128K Instruct

plain_description: Alibaba Cloud's Qwen3 family delivers enterprise-grade AI reasoning, coding, and agent capabilities — all in one open-source model family. It handles complex problem-solving with thinking mode and fast everyday chat without, supporting 100+ languages and tool use out of the box. The bottom line: deploy state-of-the-art LLM performance on your own infrastructure or in the cloud, with models ranging from 0.6B to 235B parameters.
technical_description: Qwen3 is a family of large language models from Alibaba Cloud's Qwen team offering dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures (0.6B to 235B-A22B parameters). It provides dual-mode inference with thinking (step-by-step reasoning) and non-thinking (fast chat) modes selectable at inference time via chat template parameters. Context windows span 256K tokens, extendable to 1M tokens for long-document understanding. The models are served through Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp, Ollama, and MLX LM, each exposing OpenAI-compatible REST API endpoints. Deployment targets include NVIDIA GPUs, Apple Silicon, Intel CPUs via OpenVINO, Ascend NPUs via MindIE, and mobile/edge devices via ExecuTorch and MNN. Post-training is supported via Axolotl, UnSloth, LLaMA-Factory, and Swift for SFT, DPO, and GRPO. Tool use and function calling with MCP integration are available through Qwen-Agent.
title: Qwen3

plain_description: SmolLM gives you powerful, compact AI models for text and vision that run efficiently on everyday devices, not just expensive cloud GPUs. SmolLM3 outperforms larger competitors like Llama 3.2 3B while staying fully open and customizable. The bottom line: enterprise-grade language and vision AI with complete control over deployment and data.
technical_description: SmolLM is an open-source family of small language and vision-language models from Hugging Face, built on the Transformer architecture and distributed via the Hugging Face Hub. SmolLM3, the latest 3B language model, supports dual-mode reasoning (think/no_think), multilingual inference across 6 languages, and 128K-token context windows. SmolVLM extends to multimodal tasks including visual QA and multi-image reasoning. Models are loaded through the Transformers AutoModel API and run on CPU or NVIDIA GPU hardware.
title: SmolLM
